newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: BANK TO SELL STAKE IN CZECH TV NOVA TO CME.
newsitem.headline: BANK TO SELL STAKE IN CZECH TV NOVA TO CME.

text.p: Czech savings bank Ceska Sporitelna a.s. has agreed to sell its 20 percent stake in the operator of the local TV station, TV Nova, to Nova's majority shareholder, Central European Media Enterprises Ltd. (CME), a Nova spokesman said on Tuesday.

Karel Soukup told Reuters that the acquisition had been agreed, but declined to say when the transfer would take place. It would raise Bermuda-based CME's stake in the station's operator, Ceska Nezavisla Televizni Spolecnost (CNTS), to 86 percent.
Nova is the leading Czech commercial television station launched in early 1994, with an average viewership of roughly two-thirds of television households nationwide.
CME, which has several media holdings in central Europe and former communist eastern Europe, was founded by New York cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder.
Soukup said that the transaction no longer requires approval by Czech broadcasting regulators.

"Ceska Sporitelna and CME have alread agreed about the transfer of the package of shares. From December, the Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting does not have to approve this transfer," Soukup said.
Nova raised its gross profit in 1995 to $39 million from $10 million in its inaugural year,
It is now getting increased competition from the second nationwide commercial station, TV Prima, which was reconstructed out of the struggling station TV Premiera and launched last Friday.
